{{< include ../../assets/html/edgewise-embed.html >}}

Networks with real coordinates, drawn on the map they live on.

Every figure here is live: drag a node, hover for a name, and *Open with controls* gives you the same view in a full window with the colouring and layout options exposed. The data, and the script that rebuilds each one from its source, are in the [`networks`](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks) repository.

## Chicago Neighborhoods {#chicago}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="chicago.gml"
     data-params="layout=map&colorAttr=side&edgeOpacity=0.4"
     data-caption="Chicago Neighborhoods — 77 nodes, 178 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Neighborhood (community area), positioned at its true geographic centroid |
| **An edge** | Shares a border with |

Community area boundaries and adjacency derived from the City of Chicago Data Portal (Boundaries - Community Areas, dataset igwz-8jzy). Node positions are each area's true geographic centroid (longitude/latitude); edges connect areas that share a border.

*City of Chicago · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/igwz-8jzy) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/chicago)*

**Licence.** City of Chicago Open Data Portal terms of use; published as open government data.

## UK Power Grid {#uk-power-grid}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="uk_power_grid.gml"
     data-params="layout=map&colorAttr=type&sizeAttr=degree&edgeOpacity=0.35&edgeScale=0.8"
     data-caption="UK Power Grid — 627 nodes, 752 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Substation or junction, positioned at its real coordinates |
| **An edge** | High-voltage transmission line between two substations |

High-voltage transmission grid topology extracted from OpenStreetMap by GridKit. Filtered to Great Britain (largest connected component). Node positions are real substation/junction coordinates; edge weight is the transmission line's approximate length in km.

*GridKit (Wiegmans, 2016) · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://zenodo.org/records/47317) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/uk_power_grid)*

**Licence.** Open Database License (ODbL), inherited from OpenStreetMap via GridKit (Zenodo 47317). Attribute OpenStreetMap contributors; a publicly-used derivative database must also be ODbL.

## London Underground {#london-tube}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="london_tube.gml"
     data-params="layout=map&colorAttr=line&sizeAttr=degree&edgeOpacity=0.7&edgeScale=3"
     data-caption="London Underground — 272 nodes, 313 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Station, positioned at its real coordinates |
| **An edge** | A train runs directly between these two stations (no intermediate stop) on at least one line, width ∝ number of lines sharing the segment |

London Underground network: stations (real lat/lon) and direct line-adjacency edges (two stations connected if a train runs directly between them on any line with no intermediate stop, weight = number of lines sharing that segment). Powered by TfL Open Data (api.tfl.gov.uk); contains OS data (c) Crown copyright and database rights.

*Transport for London · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://api-portal.tfl.gov.uk/) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/london_tube)*

**Licence.** Transport for London Open Data licence. TfL prescribes the attribution wording, which is carried verbatim in the attribution attribute; contains OS data (C) Crown copyright and database rights.

## NYC Subway {#nyc-subway}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="nyc_subway.gml"
     data-params="layout=map&colorAttr=route&sizeAttr=degree&edgeOpacity=0.7&edgeScale=3"
     data-caption="NYC Subway — 496 nodes, 531 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Station, positioned at its real coordinates |
| **An edge** | No other station lies between these two on the track (express skip-stops are pruned, not treated as direct connections), width ∝ number of routes sharing the segment |

NYC Subway network: stations (real lat/lon) and true physical-neighbor edges (two stations connected when no other station lies between them on the track, weight = number of routes sharing that segment) -- express-train stop patterns are pruned of the false 'skip' edges they'd otherwise create over local-only stations (see prune_express_skips in scripts/build_nyc_subway.py). Source: MTA's published GTFS static feed (web.mta.info/developers), provided for public use.

*Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://web.mta.info/developers/) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/nyc_subway)*

**Licence.** MTA open data (GTFS feeds), provided for public use.

## Tokyo Subway {#tokyo-metro}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="tokyo_metro.gml"
     data-params="layout=map&colorAttr=operator&sizeAttr=degree&edgeOpacity=0.65&edgeScale=2.3"
     data-caption="Tokyo Subway — 201 nodes, 252 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Station, positioned at its real coordinates, sized by number of connecting segments |
| **An edge** | Two stations consecutive on at least one subway line's own station list, width ∝ real peak-hour weekday trains/hour (both directions, from published timetables) |

Tokyo subway network: the 9 Tokyo Metro lines and 4 Toei Subway lines (the two operators that together make up what's commonly called the Tokyo subway). Stations (real lat/lon) and direct-adjacency edges (two stations connected when consecutive on any line's own station list, weight = number of lines sharing the segment) -- Tokyo subway lines don't skip-stop, so unlike nyc_subway.gml no express-skip pruning is needed. Edge attributes peak_trains_per_hour/avg_trains_per_hour are real weekday train frequency per segment, summed across every line sharing it, from mini-tokyo-3d's own bundled published timetables -- peak is the busiest single hour, avg is the mean over hours with any service (excludes the overnight shutdown). Source: mini-tokyo-3d's bundled data (github.com/nagix/mini-tokyo-3d, MIT license), itself derived from Japan's Public Transportation Open Data Center (odpt.org). Node attribute passengers_2021 (when present) is each station's daily boarding + alighting count, FY2021 (the most recent year in this download), from MLIT's nationwide 'Number of Passengers by Station' dataset (S12, non-commercial-use license -- see nlftp.mlit.go.jp/ksj/other/agreement.html#agree-02), joined by subway line number and Japanese station name; a station on several subway lines takes the max across its lines' own MLIT entries (see build_tokyo_metro.py for why).

*mini-tokyo-3d (Akihiko Kusanagi); MLIT National Land Numerical Information · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://nlftp.mlit.go.jp/ksj/gml/datalist/KsjTmplt-S12-v3_0.html) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/tokyo_metro)*

**Licence.** Topology MIT (mini-tokyo-3d, via the Public Transportation Open Data Center). The passengers_2021 node attribute is MLIT S12, NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY -- drop that attribute before any commercial publication.

## NYC Subway Ridership {#nyc-subway-ridership}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="nyc_subway_ridership.gml"
     data-params="layout=map&sizeAttr=total_ridership&edgeOpacity=0.15&edgeScale=0.5"
     data-caption="NYC Subway Ridership — 278 nodes, 2556 edges, directed"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Station complex, positioned at its real coordinates |
| **An edge** | A → B: estimated riders traveling from A to B, weekday PM peak (5-6pm), width ∝ ridership |

Estimated NYC Subway ridership flow between station complexes, a typical weekday PM-peak hour (Wednesday 5-6pm, June 2024) -- NOT the physical track topology (see nyc_subway.gml for that). Edge weight is MTA's own modeled 'estimated average ridership' for that hour, scaled up from OMNY/MetroCard tap data; values below 25 riders/hr are omitted to keep the dominant flows readable. Source: MTA's Subway Origin-Destination Ridership Estimate dataset, NY Open Data (data.ny.gov, resource jsu2-fbtj), provided for public use.

*Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA), via New York State Open Data · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://data.ny.gov/d/jsu2-fbtj) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/nyc_subway_ridership)*

**Licence.** MTA open data and NY State Open Data, provided for public use.
